subject.title: Bug: OpenClaw 2026.4.9 exposes agent internal thinking (English) to user

question: Should maintainers sponsor the narrow core sanitizer fix for attribute-bearing streamed thinking tags now, despite the current no-new-fix-pr and needs-security-review labels?
rationale: The source-level bug is narrow and high-confidence, but the affected boundary can expose internal reasoning to external chat recipients and the issue is already marked for security-sensitive maintainer handling.

options.title: Approve narrow sanitizer fix
options.body: Allow a focused PR that aligns the embedded stream scanner with the shared reasoning-tag grammar and adds regression tests without changing reasoning defaults or channel policy.

options.title: Keep security hold
options.body: Leave the issue open for manual security review until maintainers choose a broader reasoning-visibility policy across related channel leak issues.

options.title: Merge into broader delivery policy work
options.body: Track this only as part of the broader inter-tool delivery/leak policy issue, accepting that the attribute-tag source bug stays unresolved until that larger work lands.

recommendation.title: Approve narrow sanitizer fix
recommendation.body: Allow a focused PR that aligns the embedded stream scanner with the shared reasoning-tag grammar and adds regression tests without changing reasoning defaults or channel policy.

likelyOwner.reason: This is the best available decision owner from the history because the person has shared sanitizer history and recent main-merge context for the current review snapshot.
